title: Feature flag + staged rollout controls for tiered batching defaults
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Adds feature-flagged enablement for tiered batching defaults with staged rollout (percent + allowlists).
Adds a runtime-side kill switch to immediately revert to legacy batching behavior without redeploy.
Adds config validation and audit logging for rollout changes.
body: Summary This PR adds feature flags, staged rollout configuration, and a kill switch for enabling tiered batching defaults safely. This is plumbing only; it does not change the scheduler heuristics or knob values (those land in separate PRs). Motivation Tiered batching defaults will be rolled out gradually (internal canary → hosted subset → Dedicated opt-in). We need: (1) a single global gate, (2) a staged rollout mechanism that can be tightened to an allowlist quickly, and (3) an emergency kill switch that reverts to legacy behavior immediately when p99/queueing regressions appear. This PR implements those control-plane/runtime toggles and the precedence rules. Scope / What changed Runtime feature flag + rollout policy Added a top-level gate TieredBatchingDefaults that controls whether the scheduler will attempt to select a tiered batching profile at all. When disabled, scheduler returns legacy batching config path (existing behavior). Added staged rollout controls: rollout_percent (0-100) and allowlists (regions, route IDs, and model families). Requests are bucketed deterministically by request_id hash when rollout_percent > 0; allowlists override percent (i.e., if a route/model/region is allowlisted, it is included even if percent is 0; if a route/model/region is blocklisted, it is excluded even if percent is 100). Kill switch Introduced kill_switch_enabled (runtime config) that forces legacy batching behavior regardless of all other flags. The kill switch is read from dynamic config and takes effect without process restart. This is intended for on-call use during canary incidents. Precedence / evaluation order Implemented explicit precedence: kill switch > blocklist > allowlist > percent rollout > default disabled. This is intentionally independent of any customer-level tier override precedence (handled in ENG-18430/PR-28503). Audit logging + safety rails All changes to rollout config are audited (operator identity + change summary) in control-plane logs. Config parsing validates percent bounds, mutually exclusive allowlist/blocklist entries, and rejects unknown region strings. Added guardrails to prevent accidental full enablement: if rollout_percent > 25 in production, we require an explicit acknowledge_full_rollout=true knob in the same change set (this is enforced by config validation, not the UI). Changed areas (high-level) runtime/config tiered batching rollout policy struct + parsing runtime/scheduler feature flag check + decision point span attribute control-plane config schema + validation + audit log entry ops admin endpoint: POST /admin/runtime/rollout/batching-defaults (internal) tests unit tests for hashing determinism, precedence rules, and kill switch behavior Files changed (representative) runtime/config/feature_flags.go runtime/config/tiered_batching_rollout.go runtime/scheduler/batching_profile_selector.go controlplane/config/schema/runtime_flags.yaml controlplane/admin/handlers/rollout_batched_defaults.go runtime/tests/tiered_batching_rollout_test.go Behavior details Deterministic bucketing uses Murmur3 hash(request_id) % 100 < rollout_percent. If request_id is missing, we fall back to trace_id; if both missing, the request is treated as excluded unless allowlisted. Reason codes: this PR adds internal reason enums used for logging/trace attributes only (SelectionPath=LegacyBecauseKillSwitch, LegacyBecauseFlagDisabled, TieredBecauseAllowlist, TieredBecausePercentRollout). The public-facing reason codes emitted as metrics land in PR-28473. Operational playbook notes (for SRE/release) Canary enablement sequence recommended by SRE: start with allowlist for internal routes + a single region; then add 1-5% percent rollout for the same region; only after perf canary + error budget checks pass expand to other regions. If fast-tier p99 regresses: flip kill_switch_enabled=true, then follow up by tightening blocklist/allowlist and reverting percent to 0. Testing Unit tests: precedence matrix (kill switch beats allowlist, blocklist beats percent, etc.), percent bucketing determinism, config validation failures. Integration test: control-plane pushes dynamic config updates and runtime applies within 30s (existing dynamic config propagation). Manual test: toggled flags on staging, verified scheduler path selection via tracing attribute runtime.batching.selection_path. CI Build: pass Lint: pass Unit tests: pass Runtime integration tests: pass Notes: had one flaky dynamic-config propagation test on first run; re-run green. Screenshots / Logs (snippet) Example audit log: actor=oncall@redwood action=update_runtime_rollout target=tiered_batching_defaults diff="rollout_percent: 0→2; allowlist_routes: []→[route_chat_streaming_usw2]" Follow-ups Not included: UI surfaces for rollout config (tracked in DES-771) Not included: rollout automation hooks used by release tooling (PR-28515) Not included: metrics/alerting for rollout config changes (ENG-18429) Reviewer notes / decisions Sofia: requested precedence docs + unit tests for missing request_id fallback (addressed). Sean: asked for explicit "acknowledge_full_rollout" safety latch >25% (added in schema validation). Priya/Jordan: requested config schema naming alignment with other runtime rollouts (renamed fields from tiered_batching_rollout_* to batching_defaults.tiered.*). Merge Squash merged to main. Deployed behind flags; defaults remain disabled in production until rollout plan executes.
